sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Pain in forehead and temples, increasing
gradually at noon, of malarial origin, with vertigo and
pulsation. Worse left side. Falling in street. Inability
to remain standing. Amaurosis.

sections.label: Ears
sections.text:
Violent ringing, buzzing, and roaring in ears,
with deafness.

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Neuralgia commences tmder eye ; extends into
and around it. Pains return with great regularity; re-
lieved by pressure.

Spine. — Great sensitiveness of the dorsal vertebra;


pain on pressure. Last cervical sensitive. Pain ex-
tends to head and neck.

sections.label: Urine
sections.text:
Bloody. Turbid, slimy, clay-colored, greasy
sediment. Small amount of urea and phosphoric acid
with excess of uric acid and abundance of chlorides,
accompanied by subnormal temperature. Excessive
flow. Albuminuria.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Itching ; erythema, urticaria, icterus, vesica-
tion, pustules, purpura. Great sensitiveness. Shriveled

sections.label: Fever
sections.text: Painful swelling of various veins during a

sections.label: chill
sections.text:
Shivering even in a warm room. Anguish.
Sweat with general shivering. Trembling in limbs, with
slow pulse. Subnormal temperature.

sections.label: Relationship
sections.text:
Compare: Chin, salicyl, (Deafness,
tinnitus, and Meniere^s disease)*. Ars.; Eupat,;
Methyl, blue. Camphor mono-bromide (is said to in-
tensify the action of Quinine and render it more per-
manent.) Baja, an East Indian drug, (said to be almost
infallible in intermittent fever, quartan type) ; also Pam-
botano, Mexican remedy for intermittent and tropical
fevers.

Antidotes: Parthenum; Natr. mur.; Lach.; Am.:
